description: Create teams.py with a static name -> {id, abbreviation} crosswalk seeded from a live /teams?sportId=1 pull, so later requirements have a lookup table to resolve against.
acceptance_criteria: teams.py exists with a dict mapping full team name -> {"id": int, "abbreviation": str}
All 30 current MLB team names are present as keys, matching the exact strings returned by the MLB Stats API /teams endpoint and currentTeam.name
Abbreviation values are filled in (maintainer-supplied); at minimum the 5 sampled during design (Athletics=ATH, Pirates=PIT, Padres=SD, Mariners=SEA, Giants=SF) are correct
steps: Fetch https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/teams?sportId=1 to enumerate the 30 team name/id pairs
Write teams.py with a module-level dict (e.g. TEAM_CROSSWALK) keyed by exact API name strings, values {"id": ..., "abbreviation": ...}
Fill in abbreviation values for all 30 teams
Add/adjust type hints and a short docstring per RULES.md §3

description: Replace lookup_player_id with lookup_player_info, adding hydrate=currentTeam to the existing /people/search request so team name is available with zero extra API calls.
acceptance_criteria: lookup_player_info(name) issues exactly one HTTP request to /people/search with hydrate=currentTeam
Returns a structure containing both the numeric player id and the currentTeam name (or None/blank team_name when currentTeam is absent)
Per-run cache (_player_id_cache or equivalent) stores {id, team_name} per player name, avoiding a repeat request within the same run
All call sites previously using lookup_player_id are updated to use lookup_player_info
steps: Rename lookup_player_id to lookup_player_info; add hydrate=currentTeam to the params dict
Extract currentTeam.name (or None if the key is absent) from the response alongside player id
Update _player_id_cache to store the {id, team_name} pair keyed by player name
Update scrape_player_data (and any other caller) to use the new function and returned shape
Update test_suite.py mocks to include a currentTeam field (present and absent cases) in mocked /people/search responses

description: Resolve each player's team_name against the teams.py crosswalk and attach the abbreviation (or blank) to their compiled data dict.
acceptance_criteria: A player whose team_name matches a teams.py key gets "Team" set to the correct abbreviation
A player whose team_name does not match any teams.py key gets "Team" set to blank/empty string
A player with no currentTeam at all (team_name is None) gets "Team" set to blank/empty string
No exception is raised in either blank-cell case
steps: Import the crosswalk dict from teams.py into main.py
In scrape_player_data (or compile_player_data), look up team_name in the crosswalk and set player_data["Team"] to the abbreviation or "" if not found
Keep this resolution step separate from cache-writing logic (requirement 5/6) so it can be unit tested independently

description: Add a Team column to the PrettyTable output in probable_hitters, positioned immediately after Player.
acceptance_criteria: table.field_names is ["Player", "Team", "H-AB", "BB/K", "Prob %"]
Each data row's Team cell reflects player_data["Team"] (abbreviation or blank)
The separator row ("---" * len(field_names)) still renders correctly with the new column count
steps: Update table.field_names to insert "Team" after "Player"
Update the two table.add_row(...) call sites (top_players, low_players loops) to include data["Team"] in the correct position
Manually run main.py (or the test suite) to confirm the table renders with 5 columns and no misalignment

description: When a player's team_name isn't in the teams.py crosswalk, persist a review-cache entry to .cache/missing_team_cache.json instead of printing to console.
acceptance_criteria: A crosswalk miss (team_name present, not a teams.py key) writes/updates .cache/missing_team_cache.json with {team_name: {"first_seen": "YYYY-MM-DD", "players": [names]}}
A repeat miss for the same team_name appends the player's name to the existing entry's players list rather than creating a duplicate top-level key
A repeat miss for the same team_name and same player does not duplicate that name in the players list
No text is printed to the console for this case
A player with no currentTeam at all (case b, per attach-team-abbreviation-to-player-data) does NOT produce an entry in this file
steps: Add load_missing_team_cache/save_missing_team_cache helper functions (mirroring load_no_data_cache/save_no_data_cache's try/except and json.dump style) targeting .cache/missing_team_cache.json

In the team-resolution step, on a crosswalk miss with a non-None team_name, update the cache dict in memory: create the entry if absent (with first_seen = today), append the player name if not already present
Wire cache load/save into main.py's run flow (load before compile_player_data, save after), matching the existing no_data_cache pattern
Ensure the case-b path (no currentTeam) does not call this update logic at all

description: Remove a team_name's entry from missing_team_cache.json once it successfully resolves against teams.py on a later run.
acceptance_criteria: If a team_name exists as a key in missing_team_cache.json AND now resolves successfully against teams.py, that key is removed from the cache before it is saved back to disk
Team names that still fail to resolve remain untouched in the cache
The cache file is written back (via save_missing_team_cache) after any prune, so the change persists across runs
steps: After a successful crosswalk lookup for a given team_name, check if that team_name is a key in the loaded missing_team_cache dict
If present, delete it from the in-memory dict
Confirm save_missing_team_cache is called after the run so pruned state is persisted
